name: Certified in Cybersecurity
focus: Security principles, business continuity, access controls, network security, and security operations.
notes: Entry-level ISC2 credential for people starting a cybersecurity path.

name: Security+
focus: Core cybersecurity, risk, architecture, operations, and governance.
notes: Baseline SOC credential; verify regional voucher pricing before purchase.

name: GSEC
focus: Practical security fundamentals, defense, networking, cryptography, Linux, Windows, and incident handling basics.
notes: Hands-on security fundamentals credential aligned with SANS training.

name: Microsoft Security Operations Analyst Associate
focus: Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, Defender for Cloud, KQL, threat detection, and response.
notes: Best fit for SOCs using Microsoft Sentinel and Defender.

name: CySA+
focus: Security analytics, detection, vulnerability management, incident response, and reporting.
notes: Strong fit for blue-team analysts and SOC progression after Security+.

name: GCIH
focus: Incident handling, attacker techniques, detection, response, containment, and remediation.
notes: Strong incident response credential for SOC/CSIRT analysts.

name: GCIA
focus: Network traffic analysis, intrusion detection, packet interpretation, and traffic-based threat hunting.
notes: Good fit for network detection and packet-analysis-heavy SOC roles.

name: AWS Certified Security - Specialty
focus: AWS identity, logging, monitoring, infrastructure security, data protection, and incident response.
notes: Best fit for cloud security roles in AWS-heavy environments.

name: CCSP
focus: Cloud architecture, cloud data security, platform security, application security, operations, and legal risk.
notes: Good fit for cloud security engineers and security architects.

name: CISA
focus: IT audit, governance, systems acquisition, operations, resilience, and protection of information assets.
notes: Best fit for audit, compliance, assurance, and risk roles.

name: CISM
focus: Information security governance, risk management, program development, incident management, and leadership.
notes: Good management-track certification for security leaders and program owners.

name: CISSP
focus: Security and risk management, asset security, architecture, operations, IAM, testing, and software security.
notes: Widely recognized senior cybersecurity certification. Requires experience endorsement after passing.

name: GCFA
focus: Digital forensics, incident response, endpoint artifacts, timeline analysis, and threat hunting.
notes: Strong forensics and DFIR credential for advanced responders.

name: PenTest+
focus: Penetration testing, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, reporting, and remediation guidance.
notes: Useful for analysts moving toward offensive security or validation testing.

name: CEH
focus: Ethical hacking methodology, reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation concepts, and security testing.
notes: Well-known HR-filter certification. Compare against hands-on options if the role is technical.

name: OSCP
focus: Hands-on penetration testing, exploitation, privilege escalation, Active Directory attacks, and reporting.
notes: Practical offensive-security certification with a strong hands-on reputation.

name: SecurityX
focus: Enterprise security architecture, engineering, governance, risk, and advanced operations.
notes: Previously CASP+. Better aligned to senior technical security roles than entry-level SOC work.
